analysis.title: Market Resilience Holds Despite Inflation and AI Turbulence
key_insights: Siegel says the broad market has held up despite the midterm election results, concerns about AI infrastructure sustainability, the Nvidia controversy and a hotter-than-expected CPI report. He reads this as investor confidence in the economy.
Siegel expects the Fed to raise rates by 25 basis points in December. He says a 50 basis point hike is not in the cards, though he expects some officials to favor a larger move.
The latest CPI report was hotter than expected and the 10-year Treasury yield rose roughly 10 basis points on it. PPI was more in line with expectations. The 10-year yield remains around 5.13%.

Oil and gasoline have fallen substantially. WTI is about $88 a barrel and gasoline is about $3.82 a gallon, down from roughly $4.50. Wholesale prices point to about another 20 cents of relief. Siegel expects this to help headline inflation readings.

Siegel argues the US economy can withstand oil at current levels despite Iran tensions. The inflation-adjusted oil price has averaged roughly $81 to $82 over 50 years and the economy is far less oil-intensive than before. Diesel remains elevated.
Growth estimates of 2-3% point to continued expansion, which Siegel sees as support for equities despite higher rates.

Siegel says AI infrastructure earnings growth will normalize. Some companies have seen earnings double or triple and he says that cannot be extrapolated. A low forward P/E is not necessarily cheap if earnings reflect a temporary investment boom.
Nvidia faces potential regulatory and legal scrutiny over restrictions on advanced chip sales to China, and further investigations could add uncertainty.

The Anthropic IPO this week is a test of AI investment enthusiasm. Siegel expects strong demand and a quick gain for allocation holders, with volatile trading afterward. He notes SpaceX's offering was volatile after its initial surge.
Siegel remains constructive on equities and expects a favorable year-end. He says the AI sector may see further valuation adjustments that do not undermine the broader market outlook.

sector_views.rationale: Long-term AI potential is strong, but infrastructure suppliers' current earnings growth rates are cyclical and will normalize, so valuations on current earnings can mislead.

earnings_insights: Siegel says some AI-related companies have seen earnings double or triple. He says these increases cannot be extrapolated and that a low forward P/E may reflect a temporary investment boom rather than cheapness.
